newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks hold gains after Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks hold gains after Fed meeting.

text.p: Mexican stocks rose Wednesday after the Federal Reserve held U.S. interest rates steady.
"The decision came as no surprise and had been discounted by the market, but it did at least dispel some uncertainty," said Esteban Rojas, deputy research director at the Arka brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 26.54 points, or 0.79 percent, at 3,400.96. Volume was a moderate 108.2 million shares. In the broad market, gainers outnumbered losers, 45 to 33.
Policy-makers at the Fed, the U.S. central bank, left key short-term rates unchanged amid signs the U.S. economy is on course for modest growth with stable inflation next year.
Technical analysts noted that Mexico's market closed near a psychological barrier.

"We could see profit-taking between 3,400 and 3,450 points, which would help the rally to continue. Good third quarter (economic) data could help," Rojas added. Mexico's third quarter economic report is due November 26.
"The only cause for concern is the Dow. If it adjusts sharply downwards, it will hurt us. If it continues to move sideways, we see no problems," Rojas said.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 8.20 points to 6,274.24, its sixth straight record.

Among individual Mexican stocks, cement firm Cemex and phone company Telmex were notable gainers, with their CPO and L series shares up 10 centavos ($0.01) and 95 centavos ($0.12), respectively, at 28.40 ($3.59) and 12.60 pesos ($1.59).

"Companies that weigh heavily in the IPC, like Cemex and Telmex, have been reaching record prices. Cemex was cheap and dealers, especially foreigners, had hit it very hard because of its debt, but it's a good company," said a floor trader.
A notable loser was publishing stock Gfesa, down 11 ($0.01) centavos to 2.09 pesos ($0.26). Gfesa said it had signed a letter of intent with Bankers Trust to search for a minority partner.
"The market a little oddly to the GFesa announcement, but it is an easy stock to manipulate," said a dealer.
